title: Biology at Royal Crest: Life, up close
_note: say = text sent to ElevenLabs; cap = on-screen caption. RUD uses 'Stacy – Warm South African Female' from the account's voice list; swap voice_id for any voice in your account.

lines.say: Inside almost every cell in your body, there are about two metres of DNA.
lines.cap: Inside almost every cell in your body, there are about two metres of DNA.

lines.say: Wait. Two metres? Inside one tiny cell?
lines.cap: Wait. Two metres? Inside one tiny cell?

lines.say: Coiled up so tightly, it fits inside a nucleus too small to see.
lines.cap: Coiled up so tightly, it fits inside a nucleus too small to see.

lines.say: Welcome to the biology lab at Royal Crest Academy, in Bikita. Today: DNA, RNA, red blood cells, bacteria and viruses, in 3D.
lines.cap: Welcome to the biology lab at Royal Crest Academy, in Bikita. Today: DNA, RNA, red blood cells, bacteria and viruses, in 3D.

lines.say: Lesson one. DNA. Two strands, twisted into a double helix, like a ladder with a twist.
lines.cap: Lesson one: DNA. Two strands, twisted into a double helix, like a ladder with a twist.

lines.say: The rungs are four bases: A, T, G and C. A always pairs with T. G always pairs with C.
lines.cap: The rungs are four bases: A, T, G and C. A always pairs with T. G always pairs with C.

lines.say: So it's a code, with only four letters?
lines.cap: So it’s a code, with only four letters?

lines.say: Four letters, and three billion pairs. That's the instruction book for building you.
lines.cap: Four letters, and three billion pairs. That’s the instruction book for building you.

lines.say: Okay. So what's RNA? What's the difference?
lines.cap: Okay. So what’s RNA? What’s the difference?

lines.say: Lesson two. RNA is a working copy. The DNA unzips, and RNA copies one gene.
lines.cap: Lesson two: RNA is a working copy. The DNA unzips, and RNA copies one gene.

lines.say: RNA has one strand, not two. A different sugar, ribose. And U, uracil, takes the place of T.
lines.cap: RNA has one strand, not two. A different sugar, ribose. And U, uracil, takes the place of T.

lines.say: The copy leaves the nucleus, and a ribosome reads it, three letters at a time, to build a protein.
lines.cap: The copy leaves the nucleus, and a ribosome reads it, three letters at a time, to build a protein.

lines.say: So DNA is the master plan, and RNA is the photocopy you take to the building site.
lines.cap: So DNA is the master plan, and RNA is the photocopy you take to the building site.

lines.say: Exactly.
lines.cap: Exactly.

lines.say: Lesson three. Red blood cells. A disc, thinner in the middle, packed with haemoglobin, which carries oxygen.
lines.cap: Lesson three: red blood cells. A disc, thinner in the middle, packed with haemoglobin, which carries oxygen.

lines.say: Wait. They have no nucleus?
lines.cap: Wait. They have no nucleus?

lines.say: No nucleus, so there's more room for haemoglobin. Your bone marrow makes about two million of them every second.
lines.cap: No nucleus, so there’s more room for haemoglobin. Your bone marrow makes about two million of them every second.

lines.say: And here's the DNA link. Change one letter in the haemoglobin gene, and the cell can bend into a sickle shape. That is sickle cell disease.
lines.cap: And here’s the DNA link. Change one letter in the haemoglobin gene, and the cell can bend into a sickle shape. That is sickle cell disease.

lines.say: Lesson four. Bacteria. One single cell, with no nucleus. Its DNA floats free, in a loop.
lines.cap: Lesson four: bacteria. One single cell, with no nucleus. Its DNA floats free, in a loop.

lines.say: Look at that tail spin!
lines.cap: Look at that tail spin!

lines.say: That's a flagellum. It spins like a propeller. Some bacteria help us, like the ones that turn milk into amasi.
lines.cap: That’s a flagellum. It spins like a propeller. Some bacteria help us, like the ones that turn milk into amasi.

lines.say: Others make us sick, like cholera. That's why we boil water and wash our hands. And antibiotics can kill bacteria.
lines.cap: Others make us sick, like cholera. That’s why we boil water and wash our hands. And antibiotics can kill bacteria.

lines.say: Lesson five. Viruses. Not even a cell. Just genes, DNA or RNA, wrapped in a protein coat.
lines.cap: Lesson five: viruses. Not even a cell. Just genes, DNA or RNA, wrapped in a protein coat.

lines.say: So how does it make more of itself?
lines.cap: So how does it make more of itself?

lines.say: It can't, on its own. It locks onto one of your cells, and hijacks it to make copies.
lines.cap: It can’t, on its own. It locks onto one of your cells, and hijacks it to make copies.

lines.say: Wait. So antibiotics don't work on viruses?
lines.cap: Wait. So antibiotics don’t work on viruses?

lines.say: Correct. Antibiotics are for bacteria. For many viruses, vaccines train your body to fight back.
lines.cap: Correct. Antibiotics are for bacteria. For many viruses, vaccines train your body to fight back.

lines.say: Okay, but how small is all of this?
lines.cap: Okay, but how small is all of this?

lines.say: A red blood cell is about seven micrometres across. A bacterium, about two. A virus, about a tenth of a micrometre. And DNA is just two nanometres wide.
lines.cap: A red blood cell is about 7 µm across. A bacterium, about 2. A virus, about 0.1 µm. And DNA is just 2 nanometres wide.

lines.say: So a virus next to a red blood cell is like a football next to a house?
lines.cap: So a virus next to a red blood cell is like a football next to a house?

lines.say: Just about. That's why we need microscopes, and models.
lines.cap: Just about. That’s why we need microscopes, and models.

lines.say: So what does this mean for a child from Bikita?
lines.cap: So what does this mean for a child from Bikita?

lines.say: Biology opens doors. Doctor. Nurse. Pharmacist. Medical laboratory scientist. Biotechnologist. Vet. Agricultural scientist.
lines.cap: Biology opens doors. Doctor. Nurse. Pharmacist. Medical laboratory scientist. Biotechnologist. Vet. Agricultural scientist.

lines.say: And Zimbabwe needs every one of them, in every clinic, hospital, farm and lab.
lines.cap: And Zimbabwe needs every one of them, in every clinic, hospital, farm and lab.

lines.say: At Royal Crest, it starts in Form One. Biology, Chemistry and Physics, with real microscopes and real practicals.
lines.cap: At Royal Crest, it starts in Form 1. Biology, Chemistry and Physics, with real microscopes and real practicals.

lines.say: Science. Innovation. Skill. Taught for ZIMSEC and Cambridge.
lines.cap: Science. Innovation. Skill. Taught for ZIMSEC and Cambridge.

lines.cap: Parents: Form 1 places for January 2027 are limited.
